newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Bank Handlowy Q1 net down to PLN 145.6 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish Bank Handlowy Q1 net down to PLN 145.6 mln.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy SA, slated for flotation in June, netted 145.6 million zlotys in the first quarter of 1997, down from last year but above this year's plan, the bank said in a statement on Friday.
Handlowy said its first quarter net profit was 11 percent higher than the plan. It said it had made a net profit of 212.4 million zlotys in the first quarter of 1996.
Handlowy's total profit on banking activities amounted to 312 million zlotys and was 30 percent higher than in the same period of last year.
"All components of this result increased but the most important was an improvement in interest and exchange rate earnings," it said.
The bank said its balance sheet total increased 17 percent in the first quarter to 17.125 billion zlotys mainly due to an increase in its credit and debt instruments portfolio.
Handlowy said that after retaining a large portion of 1996 profits its shareholder equity had increased to 2.041 billion zlotys.
It had a balance sheet total of 14.676 billion zlotys and shareholder equity of 1.85 billion at the end of the first quarter of 1996.
The bank said it had maintained its high solvency ratio of 16 percent, double the central bank's minimum requirement.
Handlowy said it had also improved the quality of its credit portfolio, with its share of irregular credits down to 10.1 percent from 11.5 percent at the end of 1996.
